key_insight: A PICNN can act as the prediction step in a physics-preserving scheme for two-phase porous-media flow, while a correction step enforces thermodynamic consistency, conservation, and bounds.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical surrogate for flow solvers in reservoir and subsurface simulations, especially when permeability is discontinuous and interfacial fluxes must remain physically consistent.
method: Train a physics-informed convolutional neural network on finite-volume residuals.
Compute interfacial fluxes with TPFA using neighboring cell-centered unknowns.
Apply post-processing correction to ensure energy stability, mass conservation, and bound preservation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical results showing the finite-volume-residual-trained PICNN can replace the traditional prediction solver and outperform conventional PINNs in capturing local spatial interactions.
watch_item: Performance likely depends on accurate finite-volume residual formulation and may be sensitive to mesh quality, flux approximation, and the correction procedure's cost.
paper_title: The PICNN-Assisted Physics-Preserving Scheme for Thermodynamically Consistent Two-Phase Flow in Porous Media
